claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component state migrations are a new feature.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.

The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway, with a security group outside the component referring to the VPC.
Because the security group refers to the VPC's ID, replacing the VPC would require replacing the AWS security group too (per AWS CloudFormation docs on the security group VpcId property).
The example does not create a database.
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The second version of the example upgrades to the modern `awsx.ec2.Vpc` component while keeping the existing network.
The third version of the example removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
The resource trees for v1, v2, and v3 of the example show the tracked resource structure, with subnet named vpc-isolated-0 in v1 and vpc-isolated-1 in v2 and v3.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and components; each record has a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.
The legacy AWSX component wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components; modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts managed resources under different parents.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when saved state remains compatible, but do not remove component wrappers or transfer references.
Pulumi resource registration accepts a `stateMigrations` option taking migration callbacks, and an alias for the legacy component type lets the migration find the old component.

The migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and children) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN replacing it).
The example migration callback is safe to re-run: if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources it does nothing, and an unexpected component type raises an error.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid after migration.
The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and maps both the old component and its VPC child to the new VPC record, which keeps its AWS ID.

Pulumi runs state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration, and after both have run both callbacks return no result.

After a migration changes saved state, Pulumi compares the new program with that state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Before each upgrade in the example, `pulumi preview` should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the migration without saving it, and the update (`pulumi up`) saves the migrated state.

When users upgrade a component that registers a migration, Pulumi runs the migration automatically as part of the normal preview and update, without users writing the migration, attaching the callback, or editing stack state.
The component state migrations guide at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covers the callback contract.
The VPC example in pulumi/examples aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration contains all three programs and the migration code.
State migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi stateMigrations resource option reference at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api explains the callback API.
Component state migration state entries use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using Pulumi update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans and targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied component state migration.
